summary: Iter11 — Opportunity Radar / CATHERINE live_research market picker + normalisation. Backend pytest (15/15 passed, /app/backend/tests/test_radar_iter10.py): live_research_input() correctly (a) normalises markets string 'London' → ['London'], (b) splits CSV 'London, Berlin' → ['London','Berlin'], (c) defaults empty/None/whitespace to the 4 PRIORITY_MARKETS, (d) passes a list through unchanged, (e) always returns a search_brief that includes markets + types + date_range. Listing /api/runs?task=catherine.live_research returns 200 regardless of legacy string-markets runs; the real 4-market run da2302d0-3288-49fe-a2ba-32b5c7f41698 is retained (16 opps, 4 per_market). Legacy run 816e7eea with markets stored as the raw string 'Germany / Europe' still fetchable. Visitor header x-view-as:visitor on POST /api/run → 403. /api/mode returns owner by default; visitor header flips to 'visitor'. /api/c/opportunities returns 8 items with no mongo _id leak. Frontend (desktop 1920): /radar?as=owner after clearing localStorage radarPlan: market-picker shows the 4 PRIORITY chips (market-london-united-kingdom, market-new-york-city-united-states, market-san-francisco-bay-area-united-states, market-germany-berlin-and-other-tech-hubs-) all aria-pressed=true. Default research-query-input reads exactly 'Find developer conferences, hackathons, enterprise technology events and relevant communities across London, New York City, the San Francisco Bay Area and Germany over the next 12 to 18 months.'. Deselecting Germany updates the question to drop Germany ('across London, New York City and the San Francisco Bay Area'). market-only-london-united-kingdom gives 'across London' and turns the other 3 chips aria-pressed=false. markets-all restores all 4 to true. Adding 'Paris' via market-add-input + Enter creates market-paris chip (aria-pressed=true) and inserts into question; market-remove-paris × removes it. Reloading the page preserves 'Only London' state (localStorage radarPlan). Typing a query that mentions Germany while only London is selected shows query-mismatch warning ('Your question mentions Germany, which isn't selected…'); clicking markets-reset-query rewrites the question and surfaces query-consistent instead. Live results: latest run da2302d0 auto-renders in live-results, grouped into live-group-london-united-kingdom, live-group-new-york-city-united-states, live-group-san-francisco-bay-area-united-states and live-group-germany-berlin-and-other-tech-hubs- — exactly 4 live-result-* per group (16 total). per-market has 4 tiles; live-searched-markets lists all four full names. 'not found in a source' renders for unsourced cost. Clicking live-save-0 under the London group saves and auto-opens opp-detail-b3b920f9-2aed-4b72-b7ea-ba92248aa2d4 with location 'London', the source URL and the DIANA AgentRunCard ('Develop a campaign idea with DIANA') is present inside the detail — DIANA was NOT run. Cleanup: DELETE /api/c/opportunities/b3b920f9… → 200; opportunity count back to 8. Regression: run-history-live-research dropdown has 4 options; selecting the oldest (legacy string-markets run 8ebd8423) renders without crashing. opp-filters, opp-search, opp-tab-verified, opp-add-btn (opens opp-form), run-card-catherine-research_plan all render. /radar?as=visitor: mode-visitor banner shown, live results still render, page does not crash. Backend tests kept costs down by importing live_research_input directly instead of firing LLM runs. Only concern: one external NY-only live_research run (f166a1a7) appeared mid-session (not fired by this test) and was deleted to keep environment clean.
critical_code_review_comments: Radar.jsx groupByMarket() falls back to loose substring matching (SHORT[m] without 'the ') for grouping opportunities when x.market is not an exact market name. Works today for the four priority names but is fragile: if a user adds a custom market like 'Paris' and the LLM returns x.market='Paris, France', the group key will be 'Paris, France' and show under 'Outside selected markets' section rather than the Paris group. Low priority — matches current spec behaviour where custom markets are soft hints.

live_research_input() in server.py splits CSV by comma only. If a user types 'San Francisco, United States' as a single market, it will be split into ['San Francisco','United States'] which is wrong. Not an issue through the UI (which always sends a list) but a POST /api/run with the string 'San Francisco, United States' breaks silently. Consider only splitting on commas when the string looks CSV-y, or accept list-only in the normalised path.

No frontend-side gate on the Live search Run button in visitor mode — it will POST and the backend returns 403, which surfaces as 'Failed: Request failed with status code 403' in run-error-live-research. A pre-flight check in AgentRunCard (disable+tooltip when mode='visitor') would be a cleaner UX. Not a bug per spec ('403 toast and the page doesn't crash' — both verified).

QueryCheck PLACES regex for 'San Francisco Bay Area' is /san francisco|bay area|silicon valley/i. The computed `sel` is joined market names, so when only London is selected and the question says 'bay area', it correctly warns. But 'silicon valley' never appears in any market name so if a user explicitly selects a market named 'Silicon Valley' it would still warn. Edge-case only.
Radar.jsx is 303 lines but dense — MarketPicker + QueryCheck + PerMarket + OppRow + OppForm + Radar in one file. Splitting into components/ folder would improve readability. Not blocking.
runMarkets() in Radar.jsx handles the legacy string shape by splitting on commas — verified via dropdown selection of 8ebd8423. Good defensive coding.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (market picker, query auto-generation, mismatch warning, live-results grouping, save-and-open with DIANA card, visitor non-crash)

seed_data_creation: No permanent seed. Temporary saved opportunity b3b920f9-2aed-4b72-b7ea-ba92248aa2d4 (NDC London 2027 from the da2302d0 run) was created via live-save-0 then DELETE'd. One stray external live_research run (f166a1a7, NY-only, not created by this test session) was deleted so the real 4-market run da2302d0 remains the latest. localStorage radarPlan was cleared at start of tests. Final DB state: 8 opportunities, 4 live_research runs (same as pre-test).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Live Live research is costly — avoid firing full catherine.live_research runs. Use the da2302d0-3288-49fe-a2ba-32b5c7f41698 run as the canonical 4-market result. live_research_input() can be imported directly from backend.server for unit testing (sys.path hack in test_radar_iter10.py). The run-history dropdown is run-history-live-research with options sorted newest→oldest. Legacy runs 816e7eea (Germany / Europe) and 8ebd8423 (UK, Germany / Europe, US) are string-markets runs — keep for regression. The DIANA card inside opp-detail is not an isolated testid — detect via `text=Develop a campaign idea with DIANA` locator inside the opp-detail-{id} container.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Fix in place works end-to-end: (1) frontend market picker enforces 4 priority markets by default and feeds plan.markets as a list to catherine.live_research input, (2) backend live_research_input() normalises any shape (string, CSV, empty) to a list and injects search_brief, (3) 3×markets web max_uses and 16000 max_tokens prevent the earlier parse truncation (verified: da2302d0 has 16 opportunities and 4 per_market entries), (4) prompt is updated to make INPUT.markets authoritative over any country named in the query, (5) frontend QueryCheck surfaces mismatch warning so users notice query/market drift.
